blocks.source: Source: MLS® data from the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® and the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board, compiled by SnapStats®. Rank counts only communities with at least ten homes listed. Falling listings with steady sales mean homes are being absorbed faster; rising listings with steady sales mean more choice for buyers. A sellers’ best bet is a community where homes sell quickly against the number listed; a buyers’ best bet is the reverse. Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal.

blocks.text: Between June 2026 and September 2026, detached houses: listings fell from 78 in June to 64 in September (−17.9%), and it took 12.4% of the city’s 298 sales over the period; condos and townhomes: listings was little changed, 193 in June and 195 in September (+1.0%), and it took 19.0% of the city’s 558 sales over the period.
The monthly write-ups singled out Langley City for detached houses in July (a buyers’ best bet); condos and townhomes in June, August (a buyers’ best bet).

Condo buildings in Langley City
Parkway Estates — 5360 205 Street, Langley City

Built 1988, 54 units (building directory, secondary source). The directory records the restrictions as: age restrictions, pets not allowed, rentals not allowed — the rental line is VOID since November 24, 2022. Amenities listed: elevator, guest suite, in-suite laundry, recreation centre, storage, wheelchair access. Listings describe the community as 55+ (Parkway).
Parkway II — 5363 206 Street, Langley City

Built 1989, 42 units (building directory, secondary source). The directory records the same restriction set: age restrictions, pets not allowed, rentals not allowed — the rental line is VOID since November 24, 2022. Amenities listed: elevator, guest suite, in-suite laundry, recreation centre, wheelchair access, workshop. Listings describe it as a 55+ community ("Parkway II" / "Parkway Two") whose strata fee covers hot water, gas, electricity and heat, with a recently completed full roof replacement stated in one listing — a listing claim, not a verified strata record.
Glenmont Park — 5375 205 Street, Langley City

Built 1990, 3 storeys, wood-frame construction (listing data). A full MLS data sheet for a unit in the building records "Units in Strata: 43," a 55+ age restriction, and no cats and no dogs permitted; listings describe a 55+ community whose strata fee includes electricity, gas and hot water, with a guest suite, workshop, clubhouse and RV parking. Unit count is from that MLS data sheet (secondary source), not a building directory — treat it as published-but-single-source.

It is held here as UNCONFIRMED and is NOT counted.

items.t: What the page covers: the City of Langley as a municipality — the live page itself states "Langley City is its own municipality, separate from the Township of Langley, centred on a compact, walkable downtown," and its feed showed 252 results at reading, a snapshot, not a market statistic.

Board geography: the Langley City sub-area is one of 11 sub-areas of the Fraser Valley board community "Langley" (Aldergrove, Brookswood, Campbell Valley, County Line Glen Valley, Fort Langley, Langley City, Murrayville, Otter District, Salmon River, Walnut Grove, Willoughby Heights).

Where the condo stock concentrates: the City's verified apartment stock is a single older cluster — three 1988–1990 buildings within a few blocks of each other around 205 Street, 206 Street and 53 Avenue in the downtown core.

Langley City sub-area, September 2026 — the area's own figures (inventory / solds / sales ratio): Detached 64 / 8 / 13%; Condos & Townhomes 195 / 34 / 17% (joint with Aldergrove in the Langley set, below Murrayville 23%, Willoughby Heights 19% and Walnut Grove 18%). SnapStats publishes medians at community level only, and the only community here is the combined City + Township "Langley" — so there is NO published median for the City of Langley alone: per-sub-area medians are UNVERIFIED.

Health care: Langley Memorial Hospital, 22051 Fraser Highway — a Fraser Health community hospital with 24/7 emergency, general and internal medicine, general surgery and maternity services. The hospital's own listing places the address in the Township of Langley, immediately outside the City boundary — it is the Langleys' hospital, not a building inside the City.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in Langley City

items.t: Secondary suites (Bylaw No. 3300): a secondary suite must not exceed the lesser of 100 m² and 40% of the gross floor area of the building; the registered owner must reside on the lot; at least one extra off-street parking space is required; and the suite must be inspected, approved through a building permit and recorded in the City's secondary suites registry.

Langley City property taxes: payments received after the July 2 due date incur a penalty; the City's payment page lists City Hall at 20399 Douglas Crescent and a 2.2% processing fee on credit-card payments. The penalty percentage for Langley City 2026: UNVERIFIED — the City page read states that a penalty applies but does not state the rate.

blocks.text: Good to know about Langley City

items.t: A count of "6 City condo buildings" assembled by adding the two files together would be double-counting.

Parkway Estates (1988), Parkway II (1989) and Glenmont Park (1990) stand within a few blocks of each other around 205 Street, 206 Street and 53 Avenue, and all three are published as 55+ communities — a City condo search is, in practice, a search of those three buildings and their strata documents, whatever the 252-result feed suggests.
Its build year is itself unsettled — 1991 per listings, 1990 per the building directory.

Two addresses ten numbers apart are different buildings with different records. Glenmont Park is 5375 205 St (verified); Morningside Estates is 5365 205 St (UNCONFIRMED). Directory and listing searches blur the pair — verify the civic address on the Form B before importing any fact from one to the other.

The Langleys' hospital is not in the City. Langley Memorial Hospital's own Fraser Health listing places 22051 Fraser Highway in the Township of Langley, immediately outside the City boundary — "Langley City has the hospital" is wrong by one municipal line, even though it is the hospital City residents use.
The City's zoning bylaw is new, and its adoption date is genuinely unsettled in sources. Zoning Bylaw, 2025, No. 3300 repeals the 1996 bylaw (No.

SkyTrain is a future fact, dated by the City itself. Langley City has no station today; the City's own vision page states SkyTrain is coming "by the end of 2029" — pricing a City condo on a station that does not yet exist is pricing the City's published anticipation, not current service.
The City shelf and the Township shelf move differently.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Langley City

items.t: Zoning — City: City of Langley Zoning Bylaw 2025 No. 3300 governs the City; it repeals Zoning Bylaw 1996 No. 2100. Minimum lot sizes (Bylaw 3300, as printed): R1 Suburban Residential — 557 m² / 16 m frontage; R2 Townhouse Residential — 1,000 m², except lots created by subdivision with a registered party wall agreement (maximum 280 m², minimum frontage 4.5 m); R3 Low Rise Residential — 1,000 m² / 26.0 m. Township Bylaw 2500 does NOT apply here.

SSMUH — City: the City amended its Zoning Bylaw to permit small-scale multi-unit housing on RS1 and RS2 lots by Bylaw No. 3284, adopted June 17, 2024 — RS1/RS2 permit 4 units, and 6 units if within 400 m of a frequent bus stop. This is the CITY's own SSMUH frame; the Township's Bylaw 6020 frame is different and is never imported here.

Suites — City: a City secondary suite is capped at the lesser of 100 m² and 40% of the principal dwelling's gross floor area; the registered owner must reside on the lot; at least one extra off-street parking space is required; and the suite must be inspected, approved through a building permit and recorded in the City's secondary suites registry.

Subdivision — City: Bylaw 3300 states "No person shall subdivide land except in accordance with this bylaw"; subdivisions are subject to the City's Subdivision Control Bylaw and Development Cost Charge Bylaw; a lot created by subdivision must meet its zone's minimum lot area; and meeting the minimum standards does not bind the Approving Officer to approve. The Subdivision Control Bylaw's number: UNVERIFIED. City DCC Bylaw 2024 No. 3256.

Strata block (bare-land strata parcels, if met): Form B within 7 days, max $35 + 25¢/page; depreciation reports on a 5-year cycle for stratas with 5+ lots since July 1, 2024; minimum 10% CRF contribution since November 1, 2023; rental-restriction bylaws VOID since November 24, 2022; only 55+ age bylaws valid (SPA ss.123.1/123.2 + May 1, 2023 exemptions). A fee-simple lot carries none of this.

faq.q: Is SkyTrain coming to Langley City?
faq.a: The guide page states the Surrey Langley SkyTrain extension runs 16 km from King George Station to 203 Street in the City, with Langley City Centre Station east of 203 Street and Industrial Avenue and a current anticipated in-service date of late 2029; the City's vision page likewise states SkyTrain is coming by the end of 2029.

faq.q: Are there more or fewer homes for sale in Langley City than in June?
faq.a: In Langley City, listings of houses fell from 78 in June to 64 in September (−17.9%); condos and townhomes was little changed, 193 in June and 195 in September (+1.0%).

faq.q: How big is Langley City compared with the rest of Langley?
faq.a: In September 2026, Langley City held 14.3% of the 449 houses listed in Langley and 27.9% of the 699 condos and townhomes listed in Langley.

faq.q: How many homes sold in Langley City from June to September 2026?
faq.a: 37 houses and 106 condos and townhomes sold in Langley City over those 4 months.

faq.q: Is Langley City the same as the Township of Langley?
faq.a: No — the City of Langley is a separate municipality with its own Official Community Plan (adopted November 22, 2021) and its own Zoning Bylaw, 2025, No. 3300; the Township has its own bylaws, and the two must not be mixed.

faq.q: How many apartment-condo buildings does Langley City actually have?
faq.a: Huntsfield Green is a fourth strata name buyers meet constantly, but it is townhouse-form and is not an apartment condo. Morningside Estates (5365 205 St) and the Unity Building (20769 Fraser Hwy) are UNCONFIRMED and are not counted.

faq.q: The Parkway directory says rentals are banned and it's 55+. Which one binds me?
faq.a: The rental line does not — rental-restriction bylaws have been void since November 24, 2022. The 55+ line can: a 55-or-older bylaw is the one age bylaw the Strata Property Act still permits (ss. 123.1/123.2), with exemptions for legacy residents, live-in caregivers and (since May 1, 2023) younger spouses/partners and defined children. Both Parkway buildings are directory-recorded with age restrictions, pets not allowed and rentals not allowed; read only the age and pet lines as potentially live, and confirm both on the registered bylaws.

faq.q: Is Morningside Estates the same as Glenmont Park?
faq.a: No — and they must never be merged. Glenmont Park is 5375 205 St, verified, 55+, 43 units in strata per an MLS data sheet.

faq.q: What about the Unity Building on Fraser Highway — why isn't it in the roster?
faq.a: Because listing text is not verification.

faq.q: Is Langley City the same market as the Township of Langley?
faq.a: No — separate municipalities, separate OCPs and zoning bylaws.

faq.q: Is Huntsfield Green a condo or a townhouse complex?
faq.a: Townhouse-form — gated rancher/bungalow townhouses, strata plan NWS3354, verified 55+. Its build year is UNCONFIRMED between 1990 and 1991.

faq.q: Is the Unity Building a townhouse complex?
faq.a: No. Fresh verification confirms apartment form: 5 floors of Apartment/Condo residences over commercial retail at 20769 Fraser Highway, built 2026 by Whitetail Homes.
